title: Optimize NCCL overlap and kernel scheduling for tensor-parallel collectives
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Tensor-parallel (TP) workloads were frequently bottlenecked by suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU compute. In production traces we observed kernel launch synchronization points and cross-stream barriers that prevented NCCL communication from progressing concurrently with compute, resulting in lower throughput and higher tail latency on multi-GPU TP instances. This PR introduces a combination of scheduler-level and kernel-launch changes to improve comm/compute overlap, plus KV-cache and continuous-batching alignment to maximize effective batching across microbatches. Key changes: 1) Add NcclStreamManager: centralizes NCCL comm stream allocation and exposes prioritized stream pools (high/normal) per-device. 2) Non-blocking collective flow: move NCCL group/collective launches to dedicated comm streams and ensure kernels do not implicitly synchronize comm streams. Use ncclCommAsyncStart/End pattern where supported; fall back with careful ordering otherwise. 3) Kernel scheduling changes: reduce implicit stream waits in launcher, introduce per-kernel preferred stream hints, and minimize cudaStreamSynchronize usage inside the TP runtime path. 4) Stream priority tuning: set comm streams to high priority and offload low-priority background ops to background streams. Add heuristic to bind kernel launches that are compute-critical to normal-priority streams to avoid priority inversion. 5) KV-cache prefetch alignment: adjust continuous-batcher flush windows to emit microbatches that match the TP collective launch cadence, reducing partial-collective penalties. 6) Add runtime flags and dynamic heuristics: enable/disable async-collective path, control stream priority offsets, and a perf-mode toggle for aggressive overlap. 7) Observability: add metrics and tracing spans for comm/compute overlap, per-collective duration, and stream stall time. 8) Tests & perf harness: new unit/integration tests and a perf harness that reproducibly measures overlap improvements. Results: On internal TP perf harness (64 tokens, batch=8, 8-way TP) we see end-to-end throughput +18% and 95th-percentile token latency down 22% on A100 multi-GPU, with per-token GPU time reduced ~12%. Backwards compatibility: async-collective path is off by default and gated behind runtime flags. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag to Dedicated and Private customers for initial validation before enabling on hosted. See linked Linear tasks for rollout steps and monitoring playbook.
commits: Refactor NcclStreamManager and expose priority pools
Introduce async collective launch path and fallback path
Kernel launcher: honor stream hints and remove implicit syncs
Adjust continuous-batching flush heuristics to align with TP collectives
Add perf harness and unit/integration tests
Docs: nccl-tuning.md and runtime config docs
review_comments: Samir Patel: Left a few questions on stream lifetime management. Are we guaranteed that stream priority changes won't regress older kernels? Please add a short note about CUDA support matrix.
Ava Martinez: Reply: Added detailed CUDA support matrix to docs/perf/nccl-tuning.md and guarded priority behavior by capability checks (cudaDeviceGetStreamPriorityRange) in NcclStreamManager.
Jordan Liu: The async path looks good but I saw one test flake on CI where NCCL group ordering had a race. Recommend adding an explicit ordering fence when falling back on older NCCL versions.
Ava Martinez: Reply: Added version-gated fence path and unit test that reproduces the ordering case. Also added a CI-only stress test to catch regressions.
Priya Rao: Please add an opt-out runtime flag for Dedicated customers to disable the new heuristic until we complete capacity validation.
Ava Martinez: Reply: Added runtime flag runtime.enable_tp_async_collectives and documented rollout steps. Flag is off by default in hosted.
Samir Patel: Approved after addressing comments and CI green.
release_notes: Performance: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput by optimizing NCCL overlap and kernel scheduling; reduced tail latency. Features: NcclStreamManager and runtime flags to control async collectives and stream priorities; KV-cache and continuous-batching alignment. Docs: Added nccl tuning guidance. Rollout: gated behind runtime flag and staged rollout for Dedicated/Private.
notes_for_oncall: If regressions appear after rollout: disable runtime.enable_tp_async_collectives, collect NCCL traces (nvtx/NCCL_TRACE), upload perf-harness traces, and revert to previous config via console. Playbook linked in ENG-8271.
perf_numbers: internal-harness: 8-way TP, batch=8, seq=64 on A100: throughput +18%, p95 token latency -22%, per-token GPU time -12% (compared to baseline)
